title: One null in my code made almost half of my new players quit for two weeks
author: Curious_Ad5417
selftext:
Solo dev, I make Grauwacht, a dark fantasy keep builder with guilds and raid bosses (Android and browser). I code with Claude Code, so this one is partly on both of us.

Every new player gets a short first fight, and after it a chest with their first sword should open by itself. My step counter showed something odd, 30 new players reached the end of that fight, only 15 got the chest, and 13 closed the game right there.

The cause was one line. After the fight the game called the "open chest" handler with null instead of an element. The handler reads an attribute from that element on its first line, so it threw. A try/catch around the call swallowed the error without a word. The chest did open later through a fallback, but only after a 20 second "quiet time" I had added so new players don't get flooded with popups. So right after the most exciting moment of the first minute, the screen stood still for 12 seconds. Half the players thought the game was over.

What I changed:

\- The chest now opens 0.7 seconds after the fight, and I really hope this brings back some of the new players I have been losing.

\- A test fails the build if that handler is ever called with null again.

\- The empty catch now logs, because a silent catch is just a bug with good manners.

What I learned, count every step of the first minutes. Without the step counter I would have blamed the art, the genre or the market, and never this.

AI disclosure: code with Claude Code, art and 3D beasts with AI tools, edited by me. Game design and balance are mine.

If you want to see the fixed first minute: [https://grauwacht.web.app/?von=reddit-aig5](https://grauwacht.web.app/?von=reddit-aig5)

Do you log swallowed errors in production, or did a silent catch ever cost you players?
